result.title: A Physics-Guided Transformer Framework for Electromigration Analysis in Multi-Segment Interconnects
result.summary: As technology scales to smaller nodes, increasing current densities make electromigration (EM) one of the dominant reliability challenges in on-chip interconnects. Accurate transient stress analysis is needed to identify wires susceptible to EM degradation, but applying physics-based solvers across many interconnects remains computationally expensive. This paper proposes a physics-guided transformer framework for fast EM stress prediction in multi-segment interconnect lines. The framework converts each line into geometry- and DC-aware segment tokens and uses transformer attention to capture line-level context. A lightweight query decoder then predicts stress at selected locations and time instants. The model is trained with an objective that combines normalized supervised regression, linewise relative-$L_2$ loss, and physics-guided continuity and terminal-flux terms. Experiments on IBM power grid benchmarks show that the proposed model achieves relative-$L_2$ error below 8\% and reaches up to 2459.68$\times$ speedup compared with the matrix exponential~solver.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出物理引导的 Transformer 框架，将多段互连线编码为几何与直流感知的分段 token，用注意力建模线级上下文并由轻量 query 解码器预测指定位置与时刻的电迁移应力，在 IBM 电网基准上以物理约束损失训练，取得低于 8% 的相对 L2 误差和最高 2459.68 倍加速。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是芯片互连的电迁移应力场近似求解，虽含 Transformer、token 与查询式解码等术语，但不涉及多模态视觉推理或 latent 推理状态，缺少可核查的状态、证据与决策线索，故排除。
